title: Arrows can be bent by dragging their middle
goal: An arrow can be curved: drag the handle in the middle of a selected arrow and the shaft bends into a smooth arc, the head turning to follow it, the way Keynote, Skitch and Excalidraw arrows do. Three of the four hand-made arrow references the user gave on 2026-10-01 are curved, and today every arrow is a ruler-straight line.
notes: Prerequisite for arrows-can-be-drawn-in-hand-made-styles-not-only (which depends on it for its bent-arrow acceptance items). AnnotationContent (PhotonzCore/Layer.swift) holds only start/end; arrows are drawn straight in PhotonzRender/AnnotationRasterizer.swift. The hand-made styles are written against a spine (ArrowSpine in PhotonzCore) that already accepts a quadratic curve, so the bend only has to supply the control point. References: docs/design/references/arrows/user-ref-25..28.png.
acceptance: A selected arrow shows a handle at the middle of its shaft; dragging it bends the arrow into a smooth curve that passes through the handle, and the head points along the curve where it ends
Dragging the handle back onto the straight line (or double clicking it) straightens the arrow; undo and redo step through each bend

The bend is stored on the arrow as a non-destructive property next to its start and end (PhotonzCore model + tests first), survives save, reopen, copy and SVG export, and moving either end keeps the curve’s shape
Clicking near the curved shaft selects the arrow; the layer frame grows to hold the curve so nothing is clipped

Every arrow style (Clean and the hand-made ones from arrows-can-be-drawn-in-hand-made-styles-not-only) follows the curve: Brush tapers and swells along the curve’s length, Sketch’s outline body bends with it
A walk at Next defaults draws an arrow, bends it by pointer drag on the handle, and photographs it in each style

log.note: Carries the bent half of arrows-can-be-drawn-in-hand-made-styles-not-only: every hand-made style already draws along ArrowSpine (HandMadeArrow.inks(for:along:), tested in ArrowStyleTests.everyStyleFollowsACurvedSpine); the bend only has to store a control point, pass its spine to inks/outlines/inkBounds/hit test, and extend arrow-styles-walk with a bent arrow per style.

Adversarial pass before building: a Keynote/Excalidraw user expects one mid handle that the curve passes THROUGH (not a Bezier control point off the curve), double click to reset, and the ends to keep the curve when moved; all built that way. Risk found: the handle colliding with the end handles on a short arrow, so it is only offered when it sits 20pt clear of both ends. Risk: double click on an arrow opens its caption, so the bend press is read before every double click.

Built: PhotonzCore ArrowBend + 22 core tests (ArrowBendTests) and a render test per style; app handle/drag/commit in CanvasArrowBend.swift, Straighten Arrow on right-click and Layer menu. arrow-bend-walk green (forced under a locked screen, 9 real captures, expectBox claims bent/undo/redo/straight); 19 arrow walks green, arrow-reshuffle-walk refused by the lock (needs a name). Full suite 10870 green. Left rough (no task, under the bar): Shift-even-arc has no walk; handle hides mid-drag like end handles; Hand-drawn wobble puts the dot just beside the ink; no S-curve (one handle).

Shipped 30eb1232. PhotonzCore ArrowBend: bend stored against the line between the ends (survives save, reopen, copy, SVG; moving an end keeps the shape). One spine drives the clean shaft and head, every hand-made style, frame, drawn bounds, hit test and export. Next default-on next-arrow-bend: middle handle drag bends; let go on the line, double click, or Straighten Arrow (right-click and Layer menu) straightens; one undo step each. Verified: 22 core tests plus a per-style render test, full suite 10870 green, arrow-bend-walk green at Next defaults with a pointer drag on the handle and expectBox claims (run under a locked screen, 9 real captures), 19 arrow walks green. Audit: queue/audits/2026-10-01-arrow-bend.json
